result.title: Decompose, Verify, Evolve: Physically Grounded Shape Decomposition
result.summary: Shape decomposition represents 3D objects as a compact set of geometric primitives for interpretable modeling and simulation. However, existing decomposition methods are trained primarily for geometric fidelity, without explicit constraints on physical plausibility, and can therefore produce disconnected parts or physically unstable reconstructions. We present PhysDec, an agentic framework that draws on a pretrained vision-language model's semantic understanding and commonsense reasoning to predict material-aware primitive decompositions from a few images. Within this framework, PhysDec-Loop is an agentic pipeline that reasons about part structure and materials, using a reference 3D point cloud for geometric feedback and physical verifiers to guide iterative refinement. Through self-evolution, we further develop another agentic pipeline, PhysDec-Evolved, which learns from prior corrections to predict primitive decompositions from images without point-cloud feedback or a correction loop at inference. Experiments show that PhysDec-Loop improves geometric fidelity, physical plausibility and visual quality over geometry-focused baselines, while PhysDec-Evolved approaches its performance at substantially lower inference cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PhysDec 智能体框架，利用预训练 VLM 的语义与常识从少量图像预测材质感知的几何基元分解：PhysDec-Loop 借参考点云几何反馈与物理验证器迭代修正，PhysDec-Evolved 则通过自演化把修正经验内化，在推理时无需点云反馈与修正循环。
